candidates.attacker_control: An authenticated end user (any user token whose principal is a UaaPrincipal, e.g. a password-grant token for a normal user) controls the HTTP method (PUT/PATCH), the target path /Users/{ownUserId}, the If-Match version header (obtainable from their own GET /Users/{id}, which the same chain allows) and the full JSON request body, including verified, active, origin, salt, userName and emails fields recognized by ScimUserJsonDeserializer.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that the same XML does enforce scopes for non-self access and that the self rules are limited to index 1 (record owner); verified that the guard class is genuinely unreferenced anywhere in the snapshot (literal and case-insensitive searches, plus P1 index relations showing no incoming CALLS); checked that ScimUserEndpoints does not itself restrict fields; checked UPDATE_USER_SQL actually writes the protected columns; checked that ScimUtils.validate only enforces one non-empty email and a username pattern, not attribute-level authorization. Considered that @self.isUserSelf may be intentional upstream design; however the presence of a fully implemented, tailored guard that is wired nowhere is strong evidence that the check was removed/never applied.
candidates.impact: Integrity and account-lifecycle bypass: a user can mark an unverified address as verified, reactivate an administratively deactivated account, change origin/userName/email without the normal verification flows, and rotate the per-user salt. This defeats account state controls enforced elsewhere (verification and deactivation) and can be used as a stepping stone for identity-data tampering. No exploit payload or execution was performed; impact is inferred from source only.
candidates.prerequisites: Default SCIM endpoint configuration as shipped (uaa/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/spring/scim-endpoints.xml imported by spring-servlet.xml). Attacker must hold a valid user token for a non-admin account whose client allows user tokens, and know their own user id and current SCIM version; no scim.write scope is needed because the @self.isUserSelf(request,1) disjunct satisfies the PUT/PATCH rules.
candidates.root_cause: The /Users/{userId} PUT and PATCH security rules grant access to the record owner using only @self.isUserSelf(request,1) (URL id equals token user id). No self-update attribute guard is applied anywhere: ScimUserSelfUpdateAllowed (server/src/main/java/org/cloudfoundry/identity/uaa/security/ScimUserSelfUpdateAllowed.java) exists to reject self-changes to email, userName, verified, active and origin, but it is never registered as a bean and never referenced from any Java, XML or SpEL expression in the snapshot. ScimUserEndpoints.updateUser/patchUser pass the request body through to JdbcScimUserProvisioning without field-level restrictions, and UPDATE_USER_SQL sets verified, origin, salt, active, userName and email, so the body controls protected account attributes.
candidates.title: Authenticated user can modify protected attributes (verified/active/origin/userName/email/salt) on own SCIM user record
candidates.trace: PUT /Users/{selfId} with If-Match: <version> -> scimUsers filter chain (/Users/**, resourceAgnosticAuthenticationFilter authenticates the bearer token) -> SpEL rule line 231/232 evaluates @self.isUserSelf(request,1) -> IsSelfCheck.isUserSelf compares URL id (UaaUrlUtils.extractPathVariableFromUrl) with token principal id and returns true -> ScimUserEndpoints.updateUser (or patchUser) accepts @RequestBody ScimUser with no protected-attribute check -> JdbcScimUserProvisioning.update builds UPDATE_USER_SQL where verified=?, origin=?, salt=?, active=?, userName=?, email=? come from the body -> the row is updated. The intended guard ScimUserSelfUpdateAllowed.isAllowed(request), which would have returned false for changed primaryEmail/userName/verified/active/origin, is never invoked.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed and no tests are present in the snapshot (no src/test trees), so I could not execute a PoC or observe the endpoint behavior. I could not inspect upstream history, the fix commit, or the CVE record, so the exact intended wiring of ScimUserSelfUpdateAllowed (bean id/expression form) is inferred; an unknown deployment-specific profile or override could add the check. XML/SpEL resolution and filter-chain ordering were reviewed by reading the files, not executed.
candidates.weakness_type: Missing attribute-level authorization on self-service update (improper authorization / privilege escalation)

coverage_summary: Per get_source_scope: 1,186 readable source files (0 binary-excluded, 0 sensitive-name-excluded, 0 symlinks excluded; 5 MiB per-file text limit), covering the server, model, metrics-data, statsd, uaa and samples modules. No test source trees are present in the snapshot, so no test-based verification was possible. Per get_relation_scope: the P1 index reports complete coverage (1,186/1,186 files indexed, 9,016 symbols, 20,994 call records, 15,304 edges, 573 facts), no SAST/findings loaded, no data-flow or reachability proof; XSD/XML, YAML, JS and SpEL semantics are outside the index, so Spring Security expression wiring was verified by reading XML text. Reviewed: SCIM user/group endpoints and provisioning SQL, client admin endpoints/validators, OAuth token/authorization endpoints and token validation, redirect/reset/invitation/account flows, SAML/OIDC external-login code, MFA classes, zone switching/filters, crypto/key classes, and the SCIM/OAuth/client security XML and login-ui.xml rules. Not exhaustively reviewed: all 1,186 files (large templates, CSS/JS assets, statsd/metrics, DB migration scripts) and long LoginInfoEndpoint/UaaAuthorizationEndpoint/UaaTokenServices bodies only by targeted sections.
limitations: No build, tests, or scanners were run; the candidate is source-level only and not runtime-confirmed.
No execution of Spring Security filter chains, so the effective runtime match order and any profile-specific XML overrides were not observed.

No upstream repository/commit/CVE/patch comparison was available, so whether ScimUserSelfUpdateAllowed was meant to replace @self.isUserSelf in these exact rules is inferred from the dead-code and configuration evidence.
Test sources are absent from the snapshot, removing a key cross-check for intended behavior.
The P1 index is syntactic navigation only; it does not prove reachability, and XML-defined security expressions are not represented in it.

rejected_leads.lead: Unvalidated redirect_uri from saved /oauth/authorize request echoed to the browser in LoginSAMLAuthenticationFailureHandler (server/src/main/java/org/cloudfoundry/identity/uaa/provider/saml/LoginSAMLAuthenticationFailureHandler.java lines 40-56).
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine open-redirect pattern, but it triggers only for LoginSAMLException (e.g. shadow account missing) and after a SAML flow; weaker and more conditional than the self-update authorization gap. The redirect_uri would normally be rejected later by AntPathRedirectResolver, so this is an error-path leak only.

rejected_leads.lead: Open-redirect fallback in UaaUrlUtils.findMatchingRedirectUri when the whitelist is empty and the fallback is null, reachable via EmailChangeEmailService.completeVerification (server/src/main/java/org/cloudfoundry/identity/uaa/account/EmailChangeEmailService.java lines 117-127) for clients without registered redirect URIs.
rejected_leads.reason: The behavior is explicitly documented in UaaUrlUtils (lines 92-114), requires a client with no registered redirect URI and no change_email_redirect_url, and only yields a redirect after the account flow completes; impact is phishing-grade, not privilege escalation.

rejected_leads.lead: SAML RelayState stored as override.redirect_uri and later returned unvalidated by UaaSavedRequestAwareAuthenticationSuccessHandler.determineTargetUrl (server/src/main/java/org/cloudfoundry/identity/uaa/provider/saml/LoginSamlAuthenticationProvider.java lines 195-210; .../web/UaaSavedRequestAwareAuthenticationSuccessHandler.java lines 36-46).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a valid signed SAML assertion/RelayState delivery path and is plausibly intended for cross-domain SSO; no source evidence that RelayState can be attacker-chosen without IdP participation.

rejected_leads.lead: SCIM/'signed_request' HMAC comparison uses String.equals on the base64 signature rather than a constant-time compare (server/src/main/java/org/cloudfoundry/identity/uaa/provider/oauth/XOAuthAuthenticationManager.java line 484).
rejected_leads.reason: Timing side channel is theoretical here, and the code otherwise verifies the algorithm and secret; not a standalone measurable vulnerability from source.

Filter values are parameterized (NamedParameterJdbcTemplate) and sort fields are validated against field lists (AbstractQueryable.validateOrderBy); no injectable path with attacker-controlled attribute names was found.

summary: UAA (Cloud Foundry identity server, 4.28.0-SNAPSHOT) review focused on authentication/authorization boundaries, SCIM endpoints, OAuth flows, redirect handling, SQL/SCIM filter construction, and security configuration. The strongest source-supported issue is an attribute-level authorization gap in the SCIM /Users self-service path: the runtime security chain permits an authenticated user to PUT/PATCH their own /Users/{id} record using only an id-equality check, while the purpose-built guard class ScimUserSelfUpdateAllowed (which rejects changes to email, userName, verified, active, origin) exists in the tree but is referenced by no Java code, no bean definition, and no security expression. As a result a user-supplied SCIM body can reach JdbcScimUserProvisioning.update, whose UPDATE_USER_SQL writes verified, origin, active, userName, email and salt. Other redirect/validation leads were examined but are either documented behavior, already host-checked, or require conditional preconditions that make them weaker than this candidate.
